- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline (e.g., 30d forecast peaks then drops), reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent periods to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops from 80+ to 70+ over 3–5 days), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias correction in 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if history shows 3+ consecutive days of price decline, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative values (e.g., -0.02 or -0.35), model often underreacts; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- When model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is trending, model often lags; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag in true price movement.
